title: The popular version. The Supreme Court ruled that Tesla invented radio.
description:
The Supreme Court ruled that Tesla invented radio. A 1984 New York Times article said the Justices overturned Marconi's patent because Tesla's work came first, according to Mercurians, which calls such accounts inaccurate.

A patent dispute, decided 21 June 1943. Marconi sued in the Court of Claims over four US patents. Chief Justice Stone wrote the opinion.

An earlier patent beat Marconi's. The Court held that Stone's patent anticipated Marconi's, and that Marconi's patent disclosed no invention over it.

One piece of the prior art. Tesla's patent disclosed a four circuit system but lacked a variable inductance for tuning. The Court said Lodge supplied it.

Marconi's original patent was not in question. The Court said his reputation as the first to achieve successful radio transmission rests on that original patent.

Nobody ruled on who invented radio. Mercurians says the Supreme Court never determined that Tesla invented radio. The ruling was about the validity of Marconi's later claims.

Tesla's name is in the ruling as prior art. Not as the winner.

Sources:
- https://www.law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/320/1: read verbatim through paragraph 80 of the opinion. Established the header (argued 9 to 12 April 1943, decided 21 June 1943, Chief Justice Stone delivering the opinion), that Marconi sued in the Court of Claims under 35 U.S.C. 68 for infringement of four patents, that the Court held Stone's patent anticipated Marconi's and that Marconi's patent disclosed no invention over Stone so the broad claims were invalid, that Tesla's patent No. 645,576 disclosed a four circuit system but lacked a variable inductance which Lodge supplied, and the sentence that Marconi's reputation as the man who first achieved successful radio transmission rests on his original patent, which is not here in question.
- https://mercurians.org/nov98/misreading.html: read in full. Established that popular accounts including a 1984 New York Times article say the Justices overturned Marconi's patent because Tesla preceded him, that the article calls such accounts in varying degrees inaccurate, and that the Supreme Court never determined that Tesla invented radio.
- https://earlyradiohistory.us/tesla.htm: first 39,953 of 132,635 characters read verbatim, remainder as a summary. Used only to confirm that the case did not try to determine who invented radio, and the quotation that the Court of Claims was right in deciding that Stone anticipated Marconi.
